title: What you're standing on (and why it's here at all)

concepts.label: Big Bang Theory
concepts.what: Universe expanded from a singularity ~13.7 billion years ago; expansion continues today; cosmic background radiation is observational evidence.

concepts.label: Nebular Hypothesis
concepts.what: Solar system formed from a rotating cloud of gas and dust contracting under gravity; sun at centre, planets from leftover disc.

concepts.label: Star Formation (Sun ignition)
concepts.what: Stars form when gas in a nebula contracts until core temperature triggers hydrogen fusion; Sun ignited ~4.6 Ga.

concepts.label: Solar System
concepts.what: Sun + 8 planets + satellites + asteroids + comets + meteoroids; formed ~4.6 Ga from solar nebula.

concepts.label: Terrestrial Planets
concepts.what: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars — small, dense, rocky, formed close to Sun where heat boiled off lighter material.

concepts.label: Jovian Planets
concepts.what: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune — large, gaseous, formed far from Sun where lighter gases survived.

concepts.label: Earth's Habitable Position
concepts.what: Earth's distance from Sun places it in the narrow band where water stays liquid long-term; precondition for life and oceans.

concepts.label: Differentiation of Earth
concepts.what: Density-driven separation of early molten Earth — heavy iron/nickel sank to form core, lighter silicates rose to form crust.

concepts.label: Moon Formation (Giant Impact)
concepts.what: Mars-sized body Theia collided with proto-Earth ~4.5 Ga; ejected debris accreted into Moon; collision set Earth's 23.5° axial tilt.

concepts.label: Degassing
concepts.what: Release of trapped gases from Earth's molten interior through volcanic vents; produced primitive atmosphere of water vapour, CO2, methane, ammonia.

concepts.label: Origin of Atmosphere
concepts.what: First atmosphere of H/He lost to solar wind; second from volcanic degassing (H2O, CO2); modern oxygen-rich atmosphere from photosynthesis.

concepts.label: Origin of Oceans
concepts.what: As Earth cooled, atmospheric water vapour condensed and rained for a long period, filling low-lying basins to form oceans.

concepts.label: Origin of Life
concepts.what: Life originated ~3.8 Ga in oceans; first organisms unicellular prokaryotes; cyanobacteria began oxygen photosynthesis ~2.5 Ga.

concepts.label: Earth's Crust
concepts.what: Outermost solid layer; continental crust 30-35 km thick (up to 70 km under mountains), oceanic crust 5-7 km thick.

concepts.label: Sial (Continental Crust)
concepts.what: Upper continental crust dominated by silica and aluminium; granitic; density ~2.7 g/cm3.

concepts.label: Sima (Oceanic Crust)
concepts.what: Lower/oceanic crust dominated by silica and magnesium; basaltic; density ~3.0 g/cm3, denser than sial.

concepts.label: Mantle
concepts.what: Layer between crust and core, ~35 km to 2,900 km depth; silicate rock rich in iron and magnesium; mostly solid, partially molten in upper reaches.

concepts.label: Earth's Core
concepts.what: Innermost layer 2,900-6,371 km; outer core liquid iron-nickel (generates magnetic field via dynamo), inner core solid iron-nickel under colossal pressure.

concepts.label: Earth's Magnetic Field
concepts.what: Magnetosphere generated by dynamo action of liquid outer core; deflects solar wind and shields surface from lethal radiation; precondition for atmosphere retention.

concepts.label: P-Waves (Primary)
concepts.what: Fastest seismic waves; longitudinal/compressional; travel through solids, liquids, and gases.

concepts.label: S-Waves (Secondary)
concepts.what: Transverse shear seismic waves; cannot travel through liquids; absence creates the shadow zone, evidencing liquid outer core.

concepts.label: Shadow Zone
concepts.what: Region 104-140 degrees from earthquake epicentre where seismic waves are not directly detected; due to refraction by liquid outer core.

concepts.label: Mohorovicic Discontinuity
concepts.what: Boundary between crust and mantle; ~35 km under continents, 5-8 km under oceans; discovered by Andrija Mohorovicic, 1909.

concepts.label: Gutenberg Discontinuity
concepts.what: Boundary between mantle and outer core at ~2,900 km depth; S-waves disappear here, indicating transition to liquid; named after Beno Gutenberg.

concepts.label: Lehmann Discontinuity
concepts.what: Boundary between liquid outer core and solid inner core at ~5,150 km depth; named after Inge Lehmann (1936).

concepts.label: Lithosphere
concepts.what: Rigid outermost shell comprising crust + uppermost solid mantle; ~100 km thick; broken into tectonic plates that float on the asthenosphere.

concepts.label: Asthenosphere
concepts.what: Zone in upper mantle ~100-410 km depth; partially molten, weak, plastic; convection currents here drive plate movement.

concepts.label: Mantle Convection Currents
concepts.what: Circular movement of mantle material driven by interior heat; hot rises, moves laterally beneath lithosphere, cools, sinks; engine of plate motion.

concepts.label: Major Tectonic Plates
concepts.what: Seven major lithospheric plates — Pacific (largest), North American, South American, Eurasian, African, Indo-Australian, Antarctic; plus minor plates.

concepts.label: Divergent Boundary
concepts.what: Plate boundary where plates move apart; magma rises from asthenosphere creating new crust; produces mid-ocean ridges and rift valleys.

concepts.label: Convergent Boundary
concepts.what: Plate boundary where plates collide; three types — oceanic-oceanic (island arcs), oceanic-continental (subduction trenches + volcanic mountains), continental-continental (fold mountains).

concepts.label: Transform Boundary
concepts.what: Plate boundary where plates slide past each other horizontally; no crust created or destroyed; causes earthquakes but no volcanism (e.g., San Andreas Fault).

concepts.label: Subduction
concepts.what: Process at convergent boundaries where denser oceanic plate sinks beneath another plate into the mantle; creates trenches and intense volcanism.

concepts.label: Mid-Ocean Ridge
concepts.what: Underwater mountain chain at divergent boundaries; longest mountain range on Earth (~65,000 km); Mid-Atlantic Ridge most prominent example.

concepts.label: Ring of Fire
concepts.what: Horseshoe-shaped zone around Pacific Ocean with intense seismic and volcanic activity; ~75% of world's volcanoes and ~90% of earthquakes.

concepts.label: Continental Drift Theory
concepts.what: Wegener's 1912 theory that all continents were once joined as Pangaea and drifted apart; evidence from coastline match, fossils, geological formations.

concepts.label: Alfred Wegener
concepts.what: German meteorologist who proposed continental drift in 1912; could not explain mechanism, so theory was rejected for half a century before being vindicated.

concepts.label: Pangaea
concepts.what: Supercontinent ~250 Ma comprising all present-day continents; began breaking apart in Triassic; first split into Laurasia (north) and Gondwana (south).

concepts.label: Panthalassa
concepts.what: Single global ocean surrounding Pangaea before continental breakup; 'all sea'.

concepts.label: Laurasia
concepts.what: Northern supercontinent from Pangaea split; comprised present-day North America, Europe, Asia; separated from Gondwana by Tethys Sea.

concepts.label: Gondwana
concepts.what: Southern supercontinent comprising South America, Africa, India, Australia, Antarctica; named after Gondwana region of India where matching Glossopteris fossils were found.

concepts.label: Tethys Sea
concepts.what: Ancient shallow sea between Laurasia and Gondwana; accumulated thick sediments over millions of years; sediments later folded and uplifted to form the Himalayas.

concepts.label: Arthur Holmes' Convection Proposal
concepts.what: 1930s proposal by Arthur Holmes that mantle convection currents could be the physical force driving continental drift; supplied the mechanism Wegener lacked.

concepts.label: Harry Hess and Sea Floor Spreading
concepts.what: 1960s discovery by Harry Hess that ocean floor is being newly created at mid-ocean ridges and spreading outward; magnetic stripes in basalt confirmed symmetric formation.

concepts.label: Plate Tectonics Theory
concepts.what: Modern theory that Earth's lithosphere is divided into rigid plates moving on the asthenosphere; absorbs continental drift; explains drift, mountain-building, earthquakes, volcanism.

concepts.label: Indian Plate
concepts.what: Tectonic plate carrying the Indian subcontinent; broke from Gondwana ~140 Ma, sprinted north at up to 15 cm/yr, collided with Eurasian plate ~50 Ma; still moving north at ~5 cm/yr.

concepts.label: India-Eurasia Collision and Himalayan Uplift
concepts.what: ~50 Ma collision of northward-drifting Indian plate with Eurasian plate; Tethys sediments compressed and lifted upward, forming Himalayas; uplift continues at ~5 mm/yr today.

concepts.label: India's Three-Zone Geological Inheritance
concepts.what: Synthesis framing — India is an assemblage of three geological inheritances: ancient Gondwanan peninsular shield (south), young Himalayan front (north), and Indo-Gangetic alluvial plain laid by rivers between them.
